answer: An important decision I currently need to make about my future is whether to pursue further studies abroad or continue building my career at home. It is a genuinely [[pivotal]] choice that will shape the next several years of my life. I need to make it because application deadlines for next year's intake are approaching, and universities will not wait for me to make up my mind. On one hand, studying abroad would offer invaluable experience and open new doors, but it is expensive and involves leaving my family. My father has recently retired, and my mother often travels to the village to look after my grandparents, so I feel a certain responsibility to be around. On the other hand, staying would mean steady progress but perhaps fewer opportunities for growth. I have a good position at my consultancy, and my manager has hinted that more responsibility may come my way soon. I need to make this decision soon, which makes it feel quite [[pressing]]. Honestly, I keep [[going back and forth]], weighing the potential rewards against the risks and sacrifices. It is a rather [[daunting]] choice, precisely because both paths have real merit. I have been seeking advice from people I trust, including my father and my elder sister, and trying to think about what truly matters to me in the long run. Whatever I decide, I want it to be a well-considered choice rather than an [[impulsive]] one. I am confident I will eventually reach a sensible conclusion, and that I will have no regrets.

followUps.q: What does your family advise you to do?
followUps.answer: My father encourages me to go, saying that he and my sister can manage things at home. My mother is more hesitant, although she would never stop me. Their support makes the decision a little easier.

followUps.q: How do you usually make big decisions?
followUps.answer: I write down the pros and cons, talk to a few people I trust, and then give myself a few days. Rushing never works for me; I need time for things to [[sink in]].

note: Added why now (deadlines), family considerations (father retired, mother caring for grandparents) and his prospects at the consultancy; plain 'sensible' unmarked, marked [[going back and forth]] and [[impulsive]].
